details.content: The rotational dynamics for a generic asymmetric aircraft are given as three differential equations for the body angular acceleration components $(\dot{p},\dot{q},\dot{r})$ in terms of the inertia determinant $T_0$ and auxiliary moment quantities $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$; the equation for the body angular acceleration component $\dot{p}$ is $T_0\dot{p} = (BC - D^2)T_1 + (FC + ED)T_2 + (FD + EB)T_3$, where the inertia determinant is $T_0 = ABC - A D^2 - B E^2 - C F^2 - 2 D E F$, where $A=I_{xx}, B=I_{yy}, C=I_{zz}, D=I_{yz}, E=I_{xz}, F=I_{xy}$, the auxiliary moments are $T_1 = (B-C)qr + (E q - F r)p + (q^2-r^2)D + L$, $T_2 = (C-A)rp + (F r - D p)q + (r^2-p^2)E + M$, and $T_3 = (A-B)pq + (D p - E q)r + (p^2-q^2)F + N$, where $L,M,N$ are the aerodynamic moments about the body axes $x_b$, $y_b$, $z_b$ respectively.

search_documents.text: KEACDE (Knowledge‑based and Extensible Aircraft Conceptual Design Environment) is implemented as a web‑based basic suite whose architecture is organized in two levels: (a) the KEACDE basic suite comprising a Knowledge Component Engine and an Extensible Basic Database and (b) higher‑level conceptual design systems constructed from the basic suite.
search_documents.title: P1

search_documents.text: The Knowledge Component Engine (KCE) provides a knowledge wrapper that enables designers to package engineering knowledge into modular "knowledge components", which contain (i) a hierarchical product data description of the design object and (ii) the methods and tools that generate or analyze that product data.
search_documents.title: P2

search_documents.text: The Knowledge Component Engine (KCE) exposes non‑programming wrapping tools: a "contents manager" to define hierarchical geometric and non‑geometric product descriptions and a "flexible extension tool" that wraps external algorithms, in‑house programs or commercial CAD/CAE software by parsing input/output files, driving programs, and by using COM interfaces or script parsing for secondary development.
search_documents.title: P3

search_documents.text: Packaged knowledge components, which contain (i) a hierarchical product data description of the design object and (ii) the methods and tools that generate or analyze that product data, are published to and retrieved from a web knowledge server
search_documents.title: P4

search_documents.text: The Extensible Basic Database is a web‑based, browser/server database framework that enables designers to construct hierarchical databases for conceptual design without programming.
search_documents.title: P5

search_documents.text: The Extensible Basic Database (EBD) supports definition and modification of hierarchical node structures, configuration of node attributes, data import/export and template management, keyword and structured searching, hierarchical and file/model/picture/video viewing, and basic numeric/character/file/model data analysis and chart/report generation.
search_documents.title: P6

search_documents.text: The Extensible Basic Database (EBD) accepts numeric, character, file, model , picture and video data

search_documents.title: P13

search_documents.title: P14

search_documents.text: The CATIA integration is achieved by the flexible extension tool, a non‑programming wrapping tool that parses input/output files and drives programs via Component Object Model (COM) interfaces or script parsing for secondary development, enabling non‑programmer designers to drive CATIA for model generation within CACDS (Civil Airplane Conceptual Design System).

search_documents.text: The inverse-advance-ratio quantity $J = nD/V$ is derived as the physically consistent primary dimensionless explanatory variable for representing propulsion effects in the conventional nondimensional body-axis aircraft force and moment coefficients.

search_documents.text: The thrust coefficient definition $C_T = T/(\rho n^2 D^4)$, with $T$ the thrust and $\rho$ the air density, with the body-axis force coefficient normalization, in which the thrust force is divided by the freestream dynamic pressure $\bar{q} = \frac{1}{2}\rho V^2$ and the wing reference area $S$, yields the propulsion component of the body x-axis force coefficient $C_{T_x,\mathrm{prop}} = 2(D^2/S)(C_{T0}J^2 + C_{T1}J + C_{T2})$, where $C_T = C_{T0} + C_{T1}J_{adv} + C_{T2}J_{adv}^2$, $J_{adv} = V/(nD)$ is the advance ratio, and $J = nD/V$ is the inverse-advance-ratio quantity.
